categories.agent-infrastructure: Harnesses, memory systems, and specifications for AI agents.
categories.lakehouse-tooling: Catalogs, engines, and libraries for working with lakehouse data.

projects.name: Pangolin
projects.tagline: A Rust-based, multi-tenant, Iceberg-compatible lakehouse catalog.
projects.description: Pangolin is a high-performance lakehouse catalog written in Rust. It supports Git-style branching, multi-tenancy, federated catalogs, and tracks any lakehouse asset type. Status: alpha.

projects.name: IceFrame
projects.tagline: A DataFrame-like Python library for Apache Iceberg tables over REST catalogs.
projects.description: IceFrame provides a DataFrame-style API for creating, reading, updating, and deleting Apache Iceberg tables through REST catalogs with local execution, plus table maintenance and export operations. Status: alpha.

projects.name: Merced AI
projects.tagline: A local-first broker for the AI agent harnesses already installed on your machine.
projects.description: Merced AI discovers agent harnesses installed locally, normalizes their noninteractive interfaces, and uses Open Agent Profile documents to create portable bots you can chat and collaborate with. It is deliberately not another agent loop: the selected harness still owns model access, tools, authentication, sandboxing, approvals, and policy enforcement.

projects.name: Loro
projects.tagline: A Python CLI agent harness for enterprise coding, governed data work, and productivity tasks.
projects.description: Loro is a Python CLI agent harness built for enterprise coding, governed data work, and productivity tasks, organized around identity, policy decisions, identity-bound approvals, sandboxed execution, and delivered audit records. The name is Spanish for parrot: a bird that listens, learns, repeats useful knowledge, and helps information move across groups.

projects.name: MagAgent
projects.tagline: A memory-first personal agent that remembers you across sessions in Git-backed Markdown.
projects.description: MagAgent is a memory-first personal agent that runs in the terminal and remembers you across sessions, keeping what it learns in Git-backed Markdown you can review. Version 1.4.0 adds per-run memory evidence, review-gated team memory, and expiring approval grants. It anchors a local-first AI productivity stack alongside MagGraph and Mag Command Center.

projects.name: MagGraph
projects.tagline: Rust-powered Markdown graph memory with search, backlinks, and recall bundles.
projects.description: MagGraph provides Markdown-based graph memory for AI agents: search, backlinks, recall bundles, and Python bindings, implemented in Rust. The name is short for Magpie, a corvid known for memory and tool use.

projects.name: Mag Command Center
projects.tagline: Cross-platform desktop cockpit for MagAgent runs, approvals, graphs, and memory.
projects.description: Mag Command Center is a cross-platform desktop application for MagAgent that brings runs, approvals, graphs, memory, plugins, and local productivity workflows into one window. It is a UI over the installed magent CLI and shares the same configuration, MagGraph memory, and plugins used from the terminal. Version 1.0.0 is the first stable release, packaged for Linux, macOS, and Windows with unsigned installers, and requires MagAgent 1.4.0.

projects.name: Agentic Graph Specification
projects.tagline: An open, implementation-neutral format for decomposing a project into a graph of agentic loops.
projects.description: The Agentic Graph Specification (AGS) defines an open, implementation-neutral format for decomposing a project into a directed acyclic graph where every node is a bounded agentic loop, one unit of work an AI agent runs end to end, and every edge is a control-flow dependency.

projects.name: Open Agent Profile
projects.tagline: An open specification for persisting a named AI agent as a file instead of a running process.
projects.description: The Open Agent Profile (OAP) defines a portable document describing a named agent: role, model, tool surface, permissions, attached context, and what previous sessions learned. Three rules make it safe to leave enabled: a profile narrows capability and never widens it, an agent cannot rewrite its own contract, and learned state is treated as untrusted content.

projects.name: Agent Approval Interchange Specification
projects.tagline: An open, transport-neutral contract for asking a human to authorize one exact agent action.
projects.description: The Agent Approval Interchange Specification (AAIS) defines the handoff when an agent runtime needs permission for an action: the request, the human decision, and the receipt. Each decision carries a digest of the exact action the person reviewed, clients may only choose scopes the harness offered, and expired, stale, or replayed decisions are rejected. The harness stays the authority while a CLI, web UI, desktop app, or policy service presents the request.

projects.name: MCP Semantic Lakehouse Demo
projects.tagline: A runnable MCP server that gives AI agents governed access to Apache Iceberg tables through a semantic layer.
projects.description: Companion code for the agenticlakehouse.com implementation patterns. PyIceberg with a local SQLite catalog, DuckDB, a YAML semantic model, and the official MCP Python SDK. Agents can list, describe, and query metrics but never write SQL; they read governed views with per-role row and column policies, and every query passes allowlists, row limits, timeouts, and a cost cap.
